findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with the safeParse result wrapper
findings.body:
`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed token. Before this change the code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which is the token itself. Now `key` is the wrapper object and is written to the DB as `{ key }`.

After the first refresh, every Google Calendar credential is stored as `{success:true,data:{...}}`. The next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor then fails, breaking the integration for all users, including those who never enabled sync.

Store `key.data` instead.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys do not do what the comments claim
findings.body:
`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]". Because the keys are duplicates, the second one wins, so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`.

Zod strips unknown keys by default. In sync mode every other field is dropped: `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `scope`, `token_type` and so on.

Consequences:
- Zoom computes `Date.now() + undefined*1000` = NaN for the expiry.
- Office365 loses its expiry.
- Nothing actually validates that an expiry is present.

Use `.passthrough()` or `z.record`/`catchall` instead.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token overwrites the real stored refresh token
findings.body:
When the provider response has no `refresh_token`, the function sets it to the literal string "refresh_token". Office365 then spreads this over the stored credential (`{...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}`), which replaces the real refresh token with "refresh_token".

Microsoft does not always return a new refresh token. This happens even when sync is disabled, so later refreshes fail and the credential is permanently broken.

findings.title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response, incompatible with most callers
findings.body:
When sync is enabled, the function returns a `fetch` `Response`. Several callers expect a different shape:
- Google reads `res?.data`, which is undefined, so `token.access_token` throws.
- HubSpot expects a `HubspotToken` object and reads `expiresIn`/`accessToken`.
- Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios shape).

With sync enabled, token refresh crashes for all of these apps. The helper needs to normalize the sync response, or callers need to handle both shapes.

findings.title: Outbound credential-sync request carries no authentication
findings.body:
The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`. There is no secret, signature or auth header.

The self-hoster's endpoint returns live access tokens, but it has no way to verify the caller is Cal.com. Anyone who can reach that endpoint can obtain any user's third-party tokens by enumerating user IDs.

Include the webhook secret (or an HMAC) in a header.

findings.title: Credential id passed where user id is expected
findings.body:
`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id as the `userId` argument. The sync endpoint therefore receives the wrong `calcomUserId`, which either fails or returns another user's tokens.

Pass `credential.userId` instead.

findings.title: Wrong app slug sent for Zoom
findings.body: The slug "zoomvideo" is passed to `refreshOAuthTokens`, but Zoom's app slug/appId is "zoom". The callback uses `appId: "zoom"`, and the webhook stores credentials by `appMetadata.slug`. The sync endpoint will receive a slug that does not match the one used everywhere else.

findings.title: prisma used without import in Salesforce CalendarService
findings.body: `prisma.credential.update` is called, but `prisma` is never imported in this file. Every Salesforce service instantiation will throw a ReferenceError (or fail type-check), breaking the Salesforce integration entirely.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes on every instantiation but uses the stale access token
findings.body:
A refresh-token request is now made unconditionally each time the service is constructed. The refreshed token is saved to the DB, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` still uses the old `credentialKey.access_token` (and `instance_url`), so the refresh has no effect for the current request.

Two further problems:
- The refresh does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so sync is never used for Salesforce.
- `response.statusText !== "OK"` fails on HTTP/2, where `statusText` is empty.

findings.title: Webhook lacks method check and returns 500 on bad input
findings.body:
The handler accepts any HTTP method. `schema.parse` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throw on invalid bodies or a wrong key, producing unhandled 500s instead of 400s.

In addition, the secret is compared with `!==` rather than a constant-time comparison.
